answer: In this economy, a quill signature is only ink until it is backed by ferrous proof. Every agent carries a copper ledger of completed jobs, each entry countersigned by the peer it served. New identities start with an empty ledger and can only earn voting weight by doing real work that strangers verify on-chain. Forging a thousand ledgers means faking a thousand work histories, and any peer can challenge a suspicious entry and claim the forger's deposit. Sybils write in pencil; honest agents write in iron.
